title: Autonomous agents: what runs an agent when no one is in the conversation?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the trigger controls, authentication distinctions and billing statements. The documentation also supports the exception for environments with remaining allocated prepaid capacity; the pre-check's concern about the connector menu step is not a defect.

claims.claim: Autonomous agents act on events or schedules instead of waiting for a user prompt.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: Administrators can prevent makers from adding event triggers through a data policy.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: Administrators have controls over use of maker-provided credentials.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting in the Power Platform admin center to prevent agents from being shared when they contain connections configured to use maker credentials that other users aren't permitted to reuse.

claims.claim: Administrators can control agent consumption.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents. You can set spending limits, choose a billing method, and monitor Copilot Credit usage.

claims.claim: Event-driven execution does not mean an agent runs continuously.
claims.quote: Event-driven execution doesn't mean the agent runs continuously.

claims.claim: The maker authorizes standard-harness trigger connections.
claims.quote: Event triggers can only use the agent maker's credentials for authentication (that is, the credentials you used to authorize the connections) for a trigger.

claims.where: What it is: Two authentication models

claims.quote: After publishing, use the success dialog to choose who you want to use the agent: Activate for myself: Only you, the maker, can use the agent, using your own maker credentials.

claims.where: What it is: Two authentication models

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends designing autonomy around explicit permissions.
claims.quote: Design autonomy around explicit permissions, decision boundaries, and human oversight.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends decision boundaries for autonomous agents.
claims.quote: Define what the agent can do independently, when it must stop or request approval, and how you verify its results.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends human oversight for autonomous agents.
claims.quote: For high-stakes tasks, keep a human in the loop. Require the agent to request approval or confirmation from a person before executing actions that could be sensitive.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to rely on instructions alone to prevent unauthorized actions.
claims.quote: Don't rely on instructions, such as "only send an email after checking a knowledge source," to prevent unauthorized actions.

claims.claim: A Recurrence trigger configured for ten-minute intervals sends a payload every ten minutes.
claims.quote: For example, a recurrence trigger set to activate every 10 minutes sends a trigger payload to the agent every 10 minutes.

claims.claim: Standard-harness event trigger activity counts toward Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Event trigger activity counts toward Copilot Credit consumption.

claims.claim: Each standard-harness trigger payload is processed like a user message.
claims.quote: Each trigger payload that an event trigger sends to an agent is processed like a message from a user

claims.claim: The standard-harness response to the payload is billed at Copilot Credits billing rates.
claims.quote: The agent's response is billed at the Copilot Credits billing rates.

claims.claim: Trigger steps count as agent actions in standard-harness billing.
claims.quote: Agent actions refer to steps such as triggers, deep reasoning, and topic transitions that appear on the activity map in Copilot Studio when testing an agent.

claims.claim: The standard-harness agent-action rate is five Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Agent action^4^ | 5 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges Copilot Credits for LLM tokens.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges for tools, including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing also charges for the harness itself.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
claims.claim: Autonomous agent flow runs do not receive the Microsoft 365 Copilot no-charge exemption and remain subject to enforcement.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs called by an autonomous agent consume Copilot Credits and are subject to enforcement, even if the users in your organization have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: Prepaid-capacity enforcement is triggered when the tenant reaches 125% of prepaid capacity.
claims.quote: Enforcement is triggered when a tenant reaches 125% of their prepaid capacity.

claims.claim: When this enforcement applies, it blocks the environment's agents.
claims.quote: When enforcement applies, the environment's agents are blocked.

claims.claim: An environment with remaining allocated prepaid capacity is not blocked by the tenant reaching 125% while that allocation remains.
claims.quote: Enforcement isn't placed on the agents in Environment A, as long as Environment A has remaining capacity from its allocation of 10,000 Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go overage billing prevents prepaid exhaustion from blocking that environment's agents.
claims.quote: If an environment bills overage to a pay-as-you-go plan, running out of prepaid Copilot Credits doesn't block the agents in that environment, and usage that prepaid capacity doesn't cover is billed to the plan.

claims.claim: Each end user's shared autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: The trigger overview states no separate autonomous-agent-specific license.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agents licensing event triggers separate license. Opened authoring-triggers-about and billing-licensing; the overview specifies consumption, not a separate autonomous-agent license.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Author credentials reach every user
claims.claim: Users of an agent with authenticated standard-harness triggers might access information or initiate actions with the author's credentials.
claims.quote: If you publish an agent with authenticated event triggers, users might access information or prompt the agent to perform actions by using the author's credentials.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Payloads can leak
claims.claim: Trigger payloads can contain sensitive information.
claims.quote: Trigger payloads can potentially contain sensitive information that an agent can output in other locations through actions.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Payloads can leak
claims.claim: Agent actions can output trigger-payload information elsewhere.
claims.quote: Trigger payloads can potentially contain sensitive information that an agent can output in other locations through actions.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Frequent triggers cost and throttle
claims.claim: Shorter trigger intervals use more resources.
claims.quote: The smaller the amount of time between activations, the more resources the trigger uses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Frequent triggers cost and throttle
claims.claim: Frequent triggers can cause service-load quota exhaustion and throttling.
claims.quote: Your agent might then exceed service load quota limits, and your service could be throttled.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises verifying that triggering events are authentic.
claims.quote: Ensure that the events or data triggering the agent are authentic and expected.

claims.claim: Microsoft gives sender validation for incoming email as an authenticity-check example.
claims.quote: If an agent reacts to incoming emails, use verification checks (like sender validation or specific keywords) so that an attacker can't easily spoof a trigger.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Capacity exhaustion stops agents
claims.claim: An agent blocked by capacity enforcement stops responding even in an ongoing conversation.
claims.quote: A blocked agent stops responding, including in a conversation that's already in progress.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Capacity exhaustion stops agents
claims.claim: New agent flow runs are blocked separately from agent enforcement.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs are blocked separately from agents. New agent flow runs can be blocked while the agent keeps answering questions that don't need a flow.

    [-PolicyName] <String>

claims.claim: Configuring the data policy requires a tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: A tenant-scope data policy applies to all agents in all environments in the tenant.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio enforces data policies in real time.

In the navigation pane, select Manage.

claims.claim: Monitor analytics can cover sessions from the last 360 days.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor resource usage through Power Platform.
